{{Short description|German mathematician}}
[[File:Dieter_Held.jpg|thumb|Dieter Held (1999)]]
'''Dieter Held''' (born 1936 in Berlin) is a German [[mathematician]].<ref name=":0">Mitgliederverzeichnis der Deutschen Mathematiker-Vereinigung e. V, 2007.</ref> He is known for discovering the [[Held group]], one of the 26 sporadic [[finite simple group]]s.<ref>Daniel Gorenstein, Finite Simple Groups, an introduction to their classification, 1982 Plenum Press, New York.</ref><ref>[[Held group]]</ref>

Held was a speaker at the 1962 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref>Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, 1962.</ref> He earned his Ph.D. in 1964 from [[Goethe University Frankfurt]], under the supervision of [[Reinhold Baer]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=21561|title=Dieter Held - the Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> From June 1965 to October 1967 Held first was lecturer at the [[Australian National University]] till July 1966 and then lecturer at Monash University, Clayton, Victoria.<ref name=":0" /> After having resigned from his position at Monash University, he returned to Germany and took up a research fellowship from the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG).<ref name=":0" /> The discovery of the Held group occurred towards the end of 1968 after he had investigated the properties of an arbitrary finite simple group having a centralizer of an involution isomorphic to that of the centralizer of an involution in the center of a Sylow 2-subgroup of the [[Mathieu group]] M<sub>24</sub> on 24 letters.<ref>Held, D. (1969a), "Some simple groups related to M<sub>24</sub>", in [[Richard Brauer|Brauer, Richard]]; Shah, Chih-Han (eds.), Theory of Finite Groups: A Symposium, W. A. Benjamin.</ref><ref>Held, Dieter (1969b), "The simple groups related to M<sub>24</sub>", Journal of Algebra, 13 (2): 253–296, doi:10.1016/0021-8693(69)90074-X, MR 0249500.</ref> Shortly afterwards [[Graham Higman]] and John McKay demonstrated that such a group exists, using a computer. This demonstration has not been published. There is a much later paper by Jörg Hrabe de Angelis showing the existence and uniqueness of the Held group.<ref>Jörg Hrabe de Angelis, A presentation and a representation of the Held group, Arch. Math., Vol. 66, 265-275 (1996)</ref>

Up to 2001, Held was professor at the Mathematics Institute of Gutenberg University in Mainz.<ref name=":0" />
